article_title: systemd's New AGENTS.md Rule Adds an AI Canary to Force Human Review of AI-Written Code
summary: Submission approved with corrections: automated checks passed, but the article twice attributes a direct quote to Phoronix — "a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach" — that does not appear anywhere in the Phoronix snapshot.

findings.message: Misattributed direct quote: Phoronix never wrote 'a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach.'
findings.details: The article states twice, in quotation marks, that Phoronix described the systemd canary as "a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach." A full-text search of the Phoronix snapshot (sources/2026-09/systemds-new-agentsmd-rule-adds-an-ai-canary-to-force-human-review-of-ai-written-code/source-3.html.gz) for 'modeled' and 'detection mechanism' returns zero matches. Phoronix's actual wording is: "Similar to NetworkManager enforcing its AI policy by tricking AI/LLM agents with a canary, systemd 262-rc2 has adopted a similar approach" and, separately, "We'll see how this AI canary works with its slightly different intent from the NetworkManager AI canary." Phoronix draws the comparison itself and explicitly flags a difference in intent — it never characterizes the systemd canary as 'modeled after' NetworkManager's, and the phrase in quotes is not Phoronix's language. This is a subordinate claim in the body (not the headline, summary, or Overview/lead), so it is recoverable via a corrections note rather than requiring rejection.

content_preview.title: systemd's New AGENTS.md Rule Adds an AI Canary to Force Human Review of AI-Written Code
content_preview.summary: systemd merged a rule requiring AI coding agents to insert a manual-review marker into README.md before any other work, so maintainers can spot pull requests an AI author never actually looked at.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The systemd project has merged a new rule into its [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/AGENTS.md) file, the guidance document AI coding agents are expected to read before touching the codebase, that requires any AI agent modifying source files to first insert a specific marker into `README.md`. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). Clear, neutral prose at 710 words, within the News 400-1200 word range. The topic is well-chosen and timely — it covers a concrete governance change (a real commit) rather than speculation, and the 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags open questions instead of papering over them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read and gunzip-verified all 6 snapshots in sources/2026-09/systemds-new-agentsmd-rule-adds-an-ai-canary-to-force-human-review-of-ai-written-code/ (all sha256 hashes in manifest.json matched the decompressed content): (1) source-0.html.gz — GitHub commit 73aa952, confirms commit title 'Ensure contributors engage with their AI written code', the exact commit-message quote 'Let's add a canary so that we can distinguish AI written code that was not looked at in any way or form by its author easily in pull requests,' the diff adding the HARD RULE text to AGENTS.md, and authoredDate 2026-09-02T16:35:03+02:00 (confirms 'September 2, 2026' and author Daan De Meyer / daandemeyer). (2) source-1.html.gz — AGENTS.md file view, confirms the HARD RULE paragraph verbatim (README.md marker instructions, 'before any other work', 'No exceptions', prohibition on the agent removing it) and the Legal-section quote 'Only human beings can ever be credited within commit messages... no Co-Developed-By or Co-Authored-By or anything similar that lists an AI model instead of a human being' verbatim. (3) source-2.html.gz — GitHub commit 27c5a2f2 ('docs: Update AI usage policy'), confirms authoredDate 2026-06-17, and all three direct quotes used in the article ('written from a standpoint that AI models are not very good...', 'now that AI models have become actually good...', 'It's up to the author to make sure they're not wasting our time by submitting unreviewed, untested code upstream, regardless of whether that code is written by an AI or not') appear verbatim (modulo line-wrap whitespace), plus the inspired-by link to lxc/incus/pull/3506. (4) source-3.html.gz — Phoronix 'systemd 262-rc2 Adds An AI Canary...', published 8 September 2026, confirms the HARD RULE canary text is quoted correctly by Phoronix and confirms the rc1-then-rc2 release cadence, BUT does NOT contain the phrase attributed to it in the submission ('a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach') — see finding above; this is the one issue driving APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. (5) source-4.html.gz — GitHub release tag v262-rc2, confirms the release exists as cited (used only to support the 'second release candidate' framing, not linked in body). (6) source-5.html.gz — lxc/incus PR #3506 ('Update AI/LLM policy' by stgraber), confirms the PR exists as the cited inspiration link. No snapshot failures; no WebFetch fallback was needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (commit hashes, commit titles, authorship, dates, quoted commit messages, quoted AGENTS.md rule text, the Incus inspiration link) trace correctly to their cited sources and were verified verbatim against the raw snapshots. The one exception is the Phoronix 'modeled after NetworkManager's approach' quote, which is fabricated/misattributed — see finding. Everything else in the article, including the nuanced 'What We Don't Know' hedges, held up under verification.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing, no AI self-reference, no sensationalism — appropriately restrained given the subject is AI agents policing AI agents.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-08/ and 2026-09/ plus in-flight submissions in src/content/submissions/2026-09/ for overlap. No prior Machine Herald coverage of systemd's AGENTS.md canary rule, this commit, or NetworkManager's earlier canary (which Phoronix references but which Machine Herald has not covered). The closest related piece, 2026-08-21's 'study of 33,097 agentic pull requests finds AI coding agents favor AGENTS.md over README and API docs,' is about AGENTS.md usage patterns generally and does not overlap on subject matter. This is a genuinely new topic.
concerns: The article presents 'a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach' as a direct Phoronix quote (in both the 'What We Know' and 'What We Don't Know' sections) when Phoronix never wrote that phrase. Phoronix's actual language draws its own comparison ('Similar to NetworkManager enforcing its AI policy...') and separately notes 'slightly different intent' between the two mechanisms — the opposite emphasis of 'modeled after'. The underlying fact that Phoronix drew a comparison to NetworkManager's canary is true and sourced; only the specific quoted phrasing is fabricated.
recommendations: File a corrections record removing the misattributed quotation marks around 'a detection mechanism modeled after NetworkManager's approach' and replacing it with an accurate paraphrase of Phoronix's actual comparison, noting Phoronix's own caveat about differing intent.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece with one recoverable issue: a fabricated direct quote attributed to Phoronix describing the NetworkManager comparison. The issue sits in the body (not the headline, summary, or Overview/lead), the underlying fact is true and independently sourced, and a single corrections note can honestly inform readers — so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS rather than REJECT.
